title: Zedekiah: “thou shalt die in peace”, or his eyes put out, bound and in prison till the day of his death?
summary: Jeremiah 34:4–5 tells Zedekiah “thou shalt die in peace” and that he will not “die by the sword”. Jeremiah 52:11 says Babylon put out his eyes, bound him in chains and put him in prison “till the day of his death”.
text: KJV Jeremiah 34:4: “O Zedekiah king of Judah” … “Thou shalt not die by the sword”. KJV Jeremiah 34:5: “thou shalt die in peace”. KJV Jeremiah 52:11: “he put out the eyes of Zedekiah; and the king of Babylon bound him in chains, and carried him to Babylon, and put him in prison till the day of his death”.
reasoning: Jeremiah 34:5 is a word of the Lord to Zedekiah king of Judah: “thou shalt die in peace”, with the burnings for his fathers and lamenting. Jeremiah 52:11 tells what Babylon did to the same king: eyes put out, bound in chains, imprisoned until death. The two can both stand if “in peace” means a death not by the sword, as 34:4 says, and not a death free of captivity. The verses quoted do not report how or where Zedekiah died, or whether the burning of odours was done for him.
scope: No tag is proposed: the record compares two statements in the KJV only. The verses quoted do not say what “in peace” covers, and they do not report Zedekiah’s death or burial. The record does not say that the word of 34:5 failed, only that the two statements read as a contrast. It does not rest on the Hebrew or the Greek.
